Balanced but cautious. The FOMC maintained a restrictive stance at 5.25–5.50% and emphasized “greater confidence” in disinflation before cuts—consistent with New Keynesian Phillips Curve evidence on inflation persistence (e.g., Galí) and inflation-forecast–targeting risk management (Svensson and Woodford). While solid growth and strong job gains are mild positives and the Committee sees risks as “better balanced,” the “lack of further progress” toward 2% and classic inflation-bias/time-inconsistency concerns argue for restraint despite the marginally dovish technical tweak of slowing Treasury redemptions. Net tone: neutral-to-slightly hawkish.
